The first lunar sample return since Luna 24 in 1976. Returned 1.731 kg of basalt from a region 1.2 billion years younger than the Apollo and Luna samples — extending the timeline of recent lunar volcanism.
First lunar sample return in 44 years (since Luna 24, 1976)
Heavy-lift backbone of the Chinese space program
China's heavy-lift pad — Long March 5 to Tianhe, Chang'e 5/6, Tianwen-1, and the lunar return programme
First soft landing on lunar far side
First-ever lunar far-side sample return. Apollo basin landing 2024-06-01 (UTC); 1935 g returned to Inner Mongolia 2024-06-25
Lander of India's Chandrayaan-2; it crashed in 2019, but the orbiter kept working

First lunar sample return in 44 years — ending a gap since Luna 24 (1976). Returned 1.731 kg from a geologically young region (2 billion years old vs 3–4 billion for Apollo samples). Rewrote our model of lunar volcanism: the Moon was geologically active much more recently than thought.

First sample return from the lunar far side — possibly the most scientifically significant lunar mission since Apollo. Far-side material (thicker crust, older surface, different composition) was completely unstudied. These samples may finally explain why the Moon's two hemispheres are so fundamentally different.
